newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Dec 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- The government had appointed two female administrative officers to assist the future Chief Executive with handover issues. But some people think the Chief Executive may not accept the arrangement.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- Taiwan's Foreign Minister John Chang said he would try all he could to safeguard Taipei's relationship with South Africa during his visit there.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- China had amended regulations to make it more convenient for Taiwanese journalists to report on the mainland.
-- China and Pakistan have agreed to establish a comprehensive cooperative relationship. Seven cooperative documents were signed during the visit of Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- A Hong Kong employee had been detained in Hunan province by the Chinese partner of his Hong Kong boss for six months because of business disputes.
-- Arts circles on the mainland are dominated by females and arts schools are having serious problems recruiting male students, who prefer to go into business to make money.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- China's housing reforms are affecting the profits of state-run enterprises listed overseas. The enterprises will be responsible for a total loss of several hundred million yuan brought about by housing reforms.
-- CITIC Pacific will actively develop its telecoms business in China with a Chinese partner. The total investment for a paging network was 300 million yuan.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The World Bank was poised to make its first investment in China's banking sector with the purchase of a stake in the private Minsheng Bank, a move that will boost international cohfidence in the banking sector.
-- Chinese investors are paying more attention to securities research, thanks to their investment maturity and to head-on competition among brokerages.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Hong Kong Futures Exchange will hold consultations this month to gauge constituents' opinions on inviting financial institutions to join as special members.
